identity: Arabic Van Dyck (Smith-Van Dyck) translation of the Gospel of Matthew, 19:27-20:34: Peter asking what the disciples will get, the parable of the labourers in the vineyard, the third passion prediction, the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and the healing of the two blind men outside Jericho. Classical scriptural prose - narrative frame plus long reported discourse, dialogue-heavy. The four <NL> breaks fall at pericope divisions, not at verse ends, so verse numbering is invisible here and only real punctuation counts. 523 real tokens.
law: Reconstruct the ink of a densely punctuated scripture edition. A boundary is a sentence-terminal mark in the printed source: full stop, question mark, exclamation. Target about 9 tokens per segment (LAW 6 classical band 6-12). CUT before every resumptive ف or ثم that opens a new narrative or explanatory step (فمضوا، فجاء، فلما، فانتهرهما، فللوقت، فإني) and before و plus a genuinely new subject or topic NP (وابن الإنسان يسلم، والعظماء يتسلطون، وأما الجلوس). DO NOT cut at (a) the colon between a speech verb and its quote - قال / فقال / قالوا / قالا / قائلين all weld forward; (b) vocative commas (يا سيد، يا ابن داود); (c) list commas and أو-chains; (d) و or ل joining verbs that share one subject, the وزرعها VP-chain exemption (وأرسلهم، ورأى، ووجد، وأخذوا، وسجدت وطلبت، وناداهما وقال، وليبذل); (e) a fronted فلما / وفيما protasis or a trailing لأن adjunct. A plain comma is not a boundary in itself; it cuts only when it separates two finite clauses with distinct subjects, which is what LAW 1 actually encodes.
reasoning: The dominant call was the speech-verb colon, which recurs about twenty times here (فقال لهم يسوع، قالوا له، قائلين، وقال). Van Dyck prints a colon at every one of them, and my LAW 0 corollary lists the colon among the marks that became boundaries (A4 title colon, J1 rubric colon). Against that I have three independent registers where the speech verb welded to its quote and my cut was scored FALSE: hadith @86 (قال ضالة الغنم قال لك أو لأخيك أو للذئب kept as ONE segment), Little Women @436 / @918 / @1033, and the Aqqad essay @976. The decisive detail sits in the hadith isnad: gold reads حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد | قال حدثنا أبو عامر - the cut lands BEFORE قال and never after it, i.e. the colon that follows a speech verb did not split even where the surrounding punctuation did. So I weld every speech frame forward and take the cut immediately BEFORE the speech verb instead (@14, @152, @158, @339, @376, @379, @511). The bet is symmetric - about 21 sites either way, F1 near 0.85 whichever side is wrong - so I let the register evidence (8+ documented false cuts of this shape, 0 documented misses) outweigh LAW 0 cut-at-coin-flips. Consequence I accept: @15-@45 (فقال لهم يسوع الحق أقول لكم إنكم ... الاثني عشر) stays a single 31-token segment and @280-@300 a 21-token one. Both are exactly one printed sentence, and my batch-1 damage came from welding ACROSS full stops, not from honouring long single sentences. I declined the second colon inside that stretch (الحق أقول لكم) for the same reason, though @20 is the site I would flip first if graded down. On commas: batch 1 shows expected commas welding at إلا أن (@503), ولكن (@1135), وهنا (@648) and وإذا (@560), so I cut at a comma only between two finite clauses with distinct subjects. That is why @300 (وابن الإنسان يسلم - new topic NP with its own predicate, C4), @307 (فيحكمون, LAW 2), @318 (وفي اليوم الثالث يقوم - fronted PP plus a subject switch from 3pl to 3sg), @384 and @390 (وبالصبغة ... تصطبغان، وأما الجلوس - fronted topic plus new predicate), @422 (والعظماء يتسلطون), @429 (بل after فلا يكون هكذا فيكم), @439 (the parallel ومن أراد) and @448 (كما, which J7 records as segment-opening and which LAW 4 would otherwise weld) all cut, while @100 (وأرسلهم), @108 (ورأى), @141 (ووجد), @190 (وأخذوا), @293 (وقال لهم) and @457 (وليبذل) do not: one subject, no new argument, the وزرعها exemption. Four low-confidence calls. @77 and @271 are gapped contrastive coordinations (وآخرون أولين / والأولون آخرين) with no verb of their own - LAW 1 wants an own predicate, LAW 3 parallelism wants a cut, LAW 0 breaks the tie toward cutting, and I treat the two sites identically rather than splitting the difference. @218 (وقد ساويتهم بنا) is formally a حال clause, which the spirit of LAW 4 would weld, but it carries a new subject (2sg addressee) and welding leaves a 15-token segment, so I cut. @471 (تبعه جمع كثير | وإذا أعميان) directly overrides my own I2, which says presentative وإذا welds; I2 came from two false cuts of mid-sentence وإذا بها / وإذا هي in an essay, whereas here وإذا introduces the two blind men as new participants at a genuine sentence break, and the clause closes with a full stop at @476. That override is register-local and low confidence. Sites I deliberately did NOT cut despite length pressure: @66 (من أجل اسمي يأخذ) is a topic-comment comma inside one clause, not a clause break, so 19:29 stays 27 tokens; @172 and @477 are fronted فلما protases - the LAW 4 mirror, where the cut goes after the adjunct and not before it; @273 is a trailing لأن adjunct; @233, @486, @499 and @515 are vocative commas; @349 (واحد عن يمينك والآخر) is an appositive pair; @121 and @165 are subjunctive result-ف inside an imperative (فأعطيكم، فتأخذوا), which is not a new narrative step. @126 (فمضوا) is kept as a one-token segment on C2 and E1 authority - short verdict and short narrative-step clauses stand alone. Free boundaries at @79, @278, @322, @462 and the final @526 are taken as given, and no boundary is placed on an <NL>. Result: 59 boundaries over 523 real tokens, 8.9 tokens per segment - inside the LAW 6 classical band and roughly three times denser than my batch-1 instinct, which is the correction LAW 0 demands.
